summary: This is an April Fools' Day RFC. It proposes two joke ways of encoding Unicode characters, UTF-9 and UTF-18, aimed at systems with 9-bit bytes or 36-bit words, which are not much used today. It humorously contrasts with the real UTF-8.

eli5.summary: This is a joke. It suggests writing letters using odd-sized chunks, as if computers still worked that way, so that old machines could join in.
